assertion.text: Erdős Problem #195: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. What is the largest $k$ such that in any permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ there must exist a monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression $x_1<\cdots<x_k$? Current best: Geneson \cite{Ge19} proved that $k\leq 5$. Adenwalla \cite{Ad22} proved that $k\leq 4$. Prize: no. Tags: arithmetic progressions.
